text: Machine learning teaches computers to learn from examples rather than following strict rules. In supervised learning, we give the computer training data, which includes input information and the correct answer for each example. For instance, we might show thousands of photos labeled either “cat” or “dog.” The computer builds a model by finding patterns in this data. Once trained, the model can make predictions about new, unseen photos. To check quality, we test the model on separate examples and calculate its accuracy. A high accuracy means the model usually chooses the right answer. As more data is added, the model often improves and becomes more reliable for real-world tasks.
